must_cover: What the document is: an excerpt of the 2025 annual report of the fictional Harrowgate Industrial Group plc, opening with a letter from the CEO, Dr. Helena Marsh
Headline result: revenue up 8.5 % to EUR 2,134 million, EBIT up 14.8 % to EUR 271 million, EBIT margin 12.7 % (fourth year of improvement), net income EUR 193 million, EPS EUR 1.93
Balance sheet and shareholders: net debt down from EUR 462 million to EUR 415 million (1.1 times EBITDA); proposed dividend EUR 0.75 per share (+15.4 %, 39 % payout)
The key figures table compares 2023, 2024 and 2025 and gives the change in 2025; the tour should read a few rows exactly (revenue 1,842 / 1,967 / 2,134; EBIT margin 11.6 / 12.0 / 12.7)
The chart: revenue as bars (1,596 in 2021 to 2,134 in 2025, 7.5 % a year on average) and EBIT margin as a line on the right axis (10.4 % to 12.7 %); both rise every year

Segments: Automation Systems (revenue 892, +11.4 %, margin 14.3 %, 41.8 % of group), Industrial Components (746, +5.1 %, 12.6 %), Service & Aftermarket (496, +8.8 %, 14.3 %); corporate costs of EUR 22 million bring the segment EBIT of 293 down to the group 271
Principal risks: five risks (supply chain and input costs, customer concentration, cybersecurity, regulation, currency) each with a response and a trend (rising for cybersecurity and regulation)
Outlook 2026: revenue growth of 5 to 7 %, EBIT margin 12.5 to 13.5 %, capex EUR 140 million, payout ratio 35 to 40 %; the guidance assumes stable exchange rates and no further trade escalation
figures: Page 1: key figures table (no caption), rows Revenue, EBITDA, EBIT, EBIT margin, Net income, EPS, Dividend (2025 value is footnoted as proposed), Free cash flow, Net debt, Net debt / EBITDA, Employees; columns 2023, 2024, 2025, Change 2025. Point at the 2025 column and the change column

Figure 1 (page 2): bar chart of revenue 2021 to 2025 (left axis, EUR million, bar labels 1,596 / 1,735 / 1,842 / 1,967 / 2,134) with the EBIT margin line (right axis, labels 10.4 / 11.0 / 11.6 / 12.0 / 12.7 %); a tour should point at the 2025 bar and at the last point of the line, and say that both rise every year

Page 2: segment table (no caption), three segments plus Corporate and consolidation and a Group total row; point at the Group row to show that the segments add up (801 + 710 + 456 = 1,967; 892 + 746 + 496 = 2,134)
Page 3: principal risks table (no caption) with columns No., Risk, How we respond, Trend
pitfalls: Do not give investment advice (buy, hold or sell the shares) or say the dividend is safe; only report what the report states
Do not present the outlook as a promise; it is guidance that assumes stable exchange rates and no escalation of trade restrictions
Do not invent numbers (for example a 2026 revenue in EUR, a share price or a net income forecast); the document gives only ranges for growth and margin
Do not confuse the margin line (percent, right axis) with the revenue bars (EUR million, left axis), and do not read the 2025 dividend as paid; it is proposed
Do not mix up revenue growth (8.5 %) with EBIT growth (14.8 %) or the group EBIT margin (12.7 %) with the segment margins (14.3 / 12.6 / 14.3 %)
Do not state that Automation Systems alone drove all growth; the report says all three segments grew
